Batch: JoeWare Unjoin, UserDump and UserName publisher source review

Scope.AdFindAcceptance: Excluded from selected acceptance batches; no AdFind action in this review.

Findings: Unjoin removes a machine from its domain locally/remotely without modifying the AD computer account; page version 1.1.0 dated 2007-07-17.
Requires Administrator rights; publisher historical platform claims are Windows 2000, Server 2003, XP and Vista; source code unavailable.

Sources.Finding: Unjoin supports remote target, credentials, reboot and timeout; -forreal is required to perform the unjoin. No host was contacted or changed.

Publisher index describes UserDump as a command-line utility to dump basic user information from NT-based systems; the product page was not available in the current publisher-page fetch. Treat the page-specific details as unverified until the page/artifact can be inspected.

Findings: UserName outputs the current user distinguished name and other identity formats; page version 1.0.0 dated 2002-10-08.
Publisher historical support is Windows 2000, Server 2003 and XP against AD; it says returned data depends on directory permissions and source code is unavailable.

Sources.Finding: UserName can output DN, SAM name, display name, unique ID, canonical name, UPN or SPN and can write an environment-variable-format command file. No live identity data was read or written.
